title: Publish exact record candidates as coherent durable transactions
statement: The Work records Module shall publish complete operational updates atomically and report durable, failed or uncertain outcomes truthfully.

what.problem: Publishing related facts separately or reporting success before commitment can expose intermediate state.
what.desired_outcome: Saved identifies a complete durable update; failed or uncertain responses remain truthful and current inspection establishes the actual state.

why.rationale: SR-044 ties success to the complete durable semantic update and checked basis, not progress through individual writes.

conditions: A freshness-checked semantic candidate is ready for atomic publication.
Publication is interrupted or a declared basis changes at a required commitment check.

contexts: IF-003 and the associated SQLite transaction; staged retained payloads use the separately defined containment and publication safeguards.

how.approach: Apply the current v4 SQLite task and maintenance contract. Use one SQLite transaction for the complete semantic update with foreign keys, WAL and full synchronization; no parallel file record journal is required.

how_much.scope: This allocation preserves its existing parent SR and accountable Module. Prior v3 file-journal mechanisms are historical at 39be9c81; current maintenance remains separately explicit.

acceptance_criteria: Use one SQLite transaction for the complete semantic update with foreign keys, WAL and full synchronization; no parallel file record journal is required.
Prepare a fitting result and validate complete candidate constraints before COMMIT.
Readers observe a coherent snapshot of authoritative current rows; related facts never appear as usable partial state.
On precommit failure roll back the task while preserving other committed work; unused staged payloads remain nonauthoritative until explicitly cleaned.
After interruption let SQLite recover the already determined committed/uncommitted outcome. Lost output alone cannot establish rollback.
Postcommit output or cleanup failure reports established committed or unknown status honestly; it does not change the engineering judgment.
constraints: Current v4 SQLite realization; source observations do not establish engineering approval or passing implementation proof.

sources.basis: Derived from SR-044 for the proposed MOD-011 responsibility. Allocates the commitment, coherent-read, read-basis recheck, and prepared-recovery contributions to all SR-044 publication paths through FUNC-046 and IF-003. AR-020 supplies safe admission and AR-022 defines explicit recovery. These criteria specify intended observations, not executed product evidence or an adoption of the REM authoring format by the CLI.

Retains the named current CLI and Record Format obligations at this allocated responsibility boundary. Their detailed formats, supported versions, limits, and observed external-edit boundaries remain authoritative; no runtime behavior or public contract is changed by this draft.

Reconcile the existing allocation with refined SR-042–044 and the explicit v4/v2 contract. Keep current-v3 byte and mutation guarantees version-scoped, preserve historical originals, and distinguish precommit recovery from committed outcome reporting. This target allocation is not runtime qualification.
